## Jurisdiction overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, barony of Cary, County Antrim
- **Main settlement:** Bushmills
- **County seat:** Carrickfergus (historic); Antrim (administrative center)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** County Antrim, province of Ulster, Ireland; after 1922, Northern Ireland (United Kingdom)
- **Population and economy:** The FamilySearch place tools do not cover Ireland — no population figure was returned by any tool. The Bushmills area is on the north Antrim coast; the local economy in this period was primarily agricultural with some linen weaving and later distilling. These are background statements, not tool-sourced findings.
- **Ethnic and religious composition:** The Ireland Church Records wiki page states that in Northern Ireland as a whole, "the Church of Ireland and various aspects of the Presbyterian Churches were the dominant religions, accounting for sixty-percent of the population in 1861," while "Catholics … accounted for forty-percent of the population." County Antrim, as a plantation county settled heavily by Scottish settlers from 1605, had a particularly strong Presbyterian community alongside the established Church of Ireland. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records

## Boundary changes

- Billy civil parish was historically part of County Antrim within the province of Ulster.
- In 1922, the island of Ireland was partitioned. The Ireland Church Records wiki page specifies that "Antrim, Armagh, Down, Fermanagh, Londonderry, and Tyrone voted to remain part of the United Kingdom." County Antrim therefore lies within Northern Ireland.
- This partition had direct archival consequences: "Separate National Archives were formed for the Republic of Ireland: the National Archives of Ireland (NAI), and Northern Ireland, Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI). Similarly civil registration became, for the Republic of Ireland, The General Register Office (GRO) and, for Northern Ireland, General Register Office (Northern Ireland) known as GRONI." Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records
- **Quirk:** Researchers must use PRONI and GRONI for County Antrim records post-1922, not the NAI or the Republic's GRO. Copies of many national records up to 1922 are available in both the NAI and PRONI.

---

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Start date:** The Ireland Church Records wiki page explicitly states "Before civil registration was introduced in 1864, Church records provide the primary source for providing baptism, marriage and burial dates." Civil registration therefore began at the all-Ireland level in 1864. For the bulk of the target period, 1780–1864, no civil vital registration existed.
- **What exists for 1864–1870:** Births, marriages, and deaths registered from 1 January 1864. Protestant (non-Catholic) marriages were registered from 1 April 1845. For Northern Ireland records from 1922, GRONI holds the originals.
- **Where held:** GRONI (General Register Office Northern Ireland) holds registrations for County Antrim. Copies up to 1922 may also be at PRONI.
- **Access:** The IrishGenealogy.ie portal (https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/en/) is listed on the Ireland Church Records page as an online access point, though it notes coverage for County Kerry, western/northwestern County Cork, and Dublin; County Antrim coverage through that portal was not confirmed by any tool result. The RootsIreland index (http://www.rootsireland.ie/, paid subscription) covers many Northern Ireland civil registration records.
- **Digitization level:** Partially indexed online; verify County Antrim coverage before searching.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church baptism, marriage, and burial registers are the primary source for 1780–1864. See Church Records below.

### Church records

This is the most important record class for the 1780–1870 period and the user's specific question about Church of Ireland registers.

#### Church of Ireland (Anglican/Episcopalian)

The Ireland Church Records wiki page provides the following grounded facts:

- "Church of Ireland Records began in 1536, but two-thirds were destroyed in 1922. This was the religion of many of the Northern Ireland London Company plantation settlers in the 17th century." Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records
- The 1922 destruction occurred at the Public Record Office in Dublin (Republic of Ireland). County Antrim is in Northern Ireland, and records held locally or deposited at what became PRONI were not destroyed in the Dublin fire. The Ireland Church Records page notes that PRONI holds Northern Ireland church records "either on microfilm or in original form."
- **PRONI's Guide to Church Records** (linked directly in the Ireland Church Records page at https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) "will help you identify what churches exist in each parish, what records exist for each church and whether the records are available in PRONI, either on microfilm or in original form." The guide covers "the majority of parishes … within the six counties of Northern Ireland" — which includes County Antrim. This is the definitive tool for confirming whether Billy/Bushmills Church of Ireland registers survive and what years they cover.
- **Digitized Church Records at PRONI:** The Ireland Church Records page links to https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1 as the access point for digitized church records held at PRONI. This is the first place to check for online access to Billy parish registers.
- **RCB Library** (Representative Church Body Library, Dublin): The Ireland Church Records page provides the address (Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14) and a link to request genealogy searches (https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy) and a list of all surviving Church of Ireland parish registers (https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf). For parishes in Northern Ireland, the registers are generally held at PRONI rather than the RCB Library, but the RCB's list confirms what survives.
- **Ffolliott Collection (FindMyPast):** The Ireland Church Records page lists three separate collections covering Church of Ireland registers: Irish Parish Register Baptisms & Confirmations (https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/irish-parish-register-baptisms-and-confirmations-ffolliott-collection), Marriages (https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/irish-parish-register-marriages-ffolliott-collection), and Burials (https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/irish-parish-register-burials-ffolliott-collection). All are paid-subscription indexes.
- **Marriage license bonds:** The Ireland Church Records page lists the FamilySearch collection "Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866" (collection ID 3460239 at https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239), described as "index & images" and free. Also listed: "Index to Church of Ireland diocesan marriage licenses, 1630–1845" in the FamilySearch Catalog (catalog ID 217297). These cover pre-civil-registration marriages.
- **Bottom line for the user's specific question:** The Billy civil parish Church of Ireland registers, if they survive, are almost certainly held at PRONI rather than the RCB Library, because the parish is in Northern Ireland. The 1922 Dublin fire did not destroy them. Consult the PRONI Guide to Church Records (linked above) to confirm which years survive and their current location, and check PRONI's digitized records portal for online access.
- **Digitization level for Church of Ireland registers:** Partially indexed (Ffolliott Collection on FindMyPast; Diocesan Marriage License Bonds on FamilySearch); original registers may be browsable via PRONI's digitized records portal.

#### Roman Catholic

- The Ireland Church Records page states: "Ireland Catholic Church Records began from the mid 1700s. Most rural parishes did not start keeping records until Catholic Emancipation in 1828. Many of the city registers date from the 1750's." Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records
- For the Bushmills/Billy area, Catholic baptism, marriage and burial records therefore likely begin around 1828 or later, given the rural character of the area.
- **Online access:** The National Library of Ireland holds Catholic registers at https://registers.nli.ie/ (free). Ancestry holds "Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915" (index and images, paid subscription: https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/).
- "Catholic and Presbyterian church registers frequently do not contain burial registers." Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records
- **Digitization level:** Indexed and images available online (NLI and Ancestry for Catholic registers covering most of Ireland).

#### Presbyterian

- The Ireland Church Records page states: "In 1605 Scottish estate owners resettled mostly Presbyterian tenants from their estates to newly established estates in Northern Ireland. Numerous registers date from the 1600's, but the average starting date for these registers is 1830." Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records
- For the Bushmills area, which was heavily settled by Scottish Presbyterian planters, Presbyterian registers are likely to exist from the early nineteenth century and possibly earlier. Presbyterian churches were the most numerous denomination in many parts of County Antrim.
- **Online access:** The Ireland Church Records page lists FindMyPast collections: Ireland Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms, Burials, Congregational Records, and Marriages (all paid-subscription indexes at FindMyPast). PRONI also holds Presbyterian registers.
- "Catholic and Presbyterian church registers frequently do not contain burial registers." Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records

#### Other denominations

Researchers should confirm their availability and online access via PRONI and the resources listed at IrishGenealogy.ie.

### Probate records

**[Tool gap]** The Ireland_Probate_Records wiki page returned only a generic stub. No probate collection was returned by any tool.

From background context: Irish probate was administered through the ecclesiastical court system (Prerogative Court and Diocesan Consistorial Courts) before 1858, and through the Principal Probate Registry and District Registries from 1858. Most pre-1922 probate records for Ireland were held in Dublin and many were destroyed in 1922. However, the Ireland Church Records page lists the FamilySearch collection "Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591–1866" at Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62077/, index and images, paid). **[Tool gap]** The Ireland_Military_Records wiki page returned only a generic stub. No military collection was returned by any tool.

Researchers should consult PRONI for locally-held muster rolls and militia records, and The National Archives (Kew, England) for British Army service records, pension files, and discharge papers relating to men from County Antrim who served in the British forces during 1780–1870 (covering conflicts including the American Revolutionary War era, Napoleonic Wars, Crimean War, and Indian campaigns). **[Tool gap]** No cemetery collection was returned by any tool. The Ffolliott Burials Collection on FindMyPast (listed in the Ireland Church Records page at https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/irish-parish-register-burials-ffolliott-collection) is a paid-subscription index that may cover Billy parish.

Departure records are scattered; the principal surviving sources are passenger manifests at the port of arrival (primarily US ports, held by NARA and accessible via Ancestry and FamilySearch), and some embarkation lists. ## Known record losses

The Ireland Church Records wiki page states that Church of Ireland records "began in 1536, but two-thirds were destroyed in 1922." The 1922 destruction occurred at the Public Record Office in Dublin (Republic of Ireland side). The page does not specifically address which individual parish registers were lost or which survived for Billy civil parish. Because County Antrim is in Northern Ireland, registers deposited at local churches or in Belfast before partition were not in the Dublin PRO at the time of the fire; survival rates for Northern Ireland Church of Ireland registers are therefore generally better than for Republic of Ireland parishes. However, confirmation of what survives for Billy/Bushmills must come from PRONI's Guide to Church Records, not from any tool result in this session.

The page also notes that the Betham, Crossle, and Thrift Genealogical Abstracts at FindMyPast were explicitly compiled as "useful substitute[s] to records lost in the 1922 Public Record Office fire." Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records

No tool result from this session states that any specific record set for Billy civil parish was destroyed or lost. Empty search results in tools that do not cover Ireland are coverage gaps, not evidence of record loss.

## Research tips

1. **Start with PRONI's Guide to Church Records** before searching any online database. The Ireland Church Records wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) states that the guide (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) identifies "what churches exist in each parish, what records exist for each church and whether the records are available in PRONI, either on microfilm or in original form" for Northern Ireland parishes. This is the definitive step for confirming whether Billy/Bushmills Church of Ireland registers survive and for what years.

2. **Search Church of Ireland records even for families who may not have been Church of Ireland.** The Ireland Church Records wiki page advises: "Search available Church of Ireland records even if your family was not of the Church of Ireland." The established church recorded baptisms, marriages, and burials for mixed or uncertain-denomination families. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records

3. **Denomination matters in County Antrim.** The Ireland Church Records page notes that "Church of Ireland and various aspects of the Presbyterian Churches were the dominant religions" in Northern Ireland (60% combined in 1861). The Bushmills area had significant Presbyterian communities descended from seventeenth-century Scottish plantation settlers. Search Presbyterian registers alongside Church of Ireland registers. The page notes that "Catholic and Presbyterian church registers frequently do not contain burial registers" — do not conclude a person died without a record simply because no Presbyterian or Catholic burial entry appears; check Church of Ireland burial registers instead. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records

4. **Identify the correct civil parish, Church of Ireland parish, and Catholic parish separately.** Civil parishes and church parishes do not share boundaries. The Ireland Church Records page advises: "Search surrounding localities if you cannot find records in the expected locality. Catholics had different parish boundaries to the Church of Ireland." Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records

5. **Civil registration began in 1864.** The Ireland Church Records wiki page states explicitly: "Before civil registration was introduced in 1864, Church records provide the primary source." For 1780–1863, the researcher must rely entirely on church records, land records, and census substitutes. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records

6. **The 1922 fire affects research strategy differently for Northern Ireland.** Two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers nationwide were destroyed in 1922, but County Antrim (in Northern Ireland) records are generally better preserved because they were not held at the Dublin PRO. Always check PRONI before concluding a register is lost.

7. **Consult genealogical abstracts for pre-1780 and fire-loss substitutes.** The Betham, Crossle, and Thrift Genealogical Abstracts (all at FindMyPast, paid) are explicitly described in the Ireland Church Records wiki page as substitutes for records destroyed in 1922. These may cover County Antrim families. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records

8. **Use the Ulster Historical Foundation for specialized Ulster research.** The Ireland Church Records wiki page lists the Ulster Historical Foundation (http://www.ancestryireland.com/) as a specialized resource for Northern Ireland genealogy, including emigration databases. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records

9. **FamilySearch wiki tool limitations for Ireland.** The place-resolution and collection-search tools used to build this guide do not support Irish jurisdictions. Researchers should consult the FamilySearch Wiki for Ireland directly at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Genealogy and browse its full list of county-level and record-type pages for County Antrim, which exist but could not be retrieved via these tools in this session.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

> **Tool-coverage notice:** FamilySearch's place-resolution tools returned no Ireland-specific results in this session. The guide below is grounded in established Irish genealogical knowledge. For current FamilySearch digitization status, consult the [Ireland Genealogy Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Genealogy) and [County Antrim Wiki page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Antrim,_Ireland_Genealogy) directly.

---

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, Barony of Dunluce North, County Antrim, Province of Ulster
- **Principal town:** Bushmills (licensed distillery from 1608; fishing village and market town along the north Antrim coast near the Giant's Causeway)
- **Economy:** Subsistence/commercial agriculture, linen manufacture, coastal fishing, whiskey distilling; dominated by tenant farmers on landlord estates
- **Denominations:** Church of Ireland (established church until 1869), Presbyterian (numerically strong; Ulster-Scots settlement), Roman Catholic, Methodist
- **Key events:** 1798 United Irishmen Rebellion (County Antrim was a major theater); Acts of Union 1800; Great Famine 1845–1852 and mass emigration; Disestablishment of Church of Ireland 1869

---

## Vital Records (Civil Registration)

Civil registration **did not exist** for the bulk of this period. Church records are the primary source.

| Event | Start date | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Non-Catholic marriages | 1 April 1845 | Registered at superintendent registrar's district (Ballycastle or Coleraine district) |
| All births, deaths & Catholic marriages | 1 January 1864 | Full system begins |

**Where held:** General Register Office of Northern Ireland (GRONI), Waterfront Plaza, Belfast. Indexes free at [IrishGenealogy.ie](https://www.irishgenealogy.ie).

---

## Church Records *(most important source class for 1780–1864)*

### Church of Ireland — Billy Parish ✅

This is the **key question** you asked about. Billy CoI parish is the ecclesiastical parish matching the civil parish.

**Survival prospects are good.** The 1922 Four Courts fire in Dublin destroyed approximately two-thirds of Irish CoI registers — but County Antrim registers were **more likely to have remained in Ulster** and were never sent to Dublin. PRONI has systematically microfilmed surviving Ulster CoI registers.

**What to do:**
1. Search the **PRONI eCatalogue** at [nidirect.gov.uk/proni](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/proni) for "Billy" under Church of Ireland records → find the MIC or CR class reference and its date range for baptisms, marriages, and burials
2. Also check the **RCB Library** (Dublin) for any diocesan copies (Diocese of Connor)
3. PRONI microfilms can be ordered as paid reproductions without visiting Belfast

### Roman Catholic

The RC population was served by separately-named parishes — likely **Ballintoy and/or Ramoan (Ballycastle)** RC parishes. RC registers in rural north Antrim typically begin in the 1820s–1840s.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

## Tool-coverage notice

All FamilySearch place-resolution tools (`place_search`, `place_search_all`, `wiki_place_page`, `wiki_read`, `collections_search`, `volume_search`) returned zero or generic results for Ireland and County Antrim in this session — "Ireland" is not being resolved as a standard place. No FamilySearch collection IDs, volume numbers, record counts, or wiki page specifics were returned. The claims below draw on established Irish genealogical knowledge; for current FamilySearch digitization status consult https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Genealogy and https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Antrim,_Ireland_Genealogy directly.

---

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy civil parish, barony of Dunluce North, County Antrim, Province of Ulster, Ireland
- **Principal town:** Bushmills (licensed distillery from 1608; fishing village and market town)
- **Other townlands:** Includes Portballintrae and numerous rural townlands along the north Antrim coast near the Giant's Causeway
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Barony of Dunluce North → County Antrim → Province of Ulster → Kingdom of Ireland / United Kingdom (from Acts of Union 1800) → Northern Ireland, United Kingdom (from 1921 partition, outside the target period)
- **Population during period:** No figure was returned by tools. County Antrim's rural north was heavily agricultural; the Great Famine (1845–1852) caused sharp population decline and emigration across the county
- **Economy:** Subsistence and commercial agriculture, linen manufacture, coastal fishing, whiskey distilling. Tenant farmers on large landlord estates dominated the social structure
- **Ethnic composition:** Ulster-Scots (Scots-Irish) Protestant settlers concentrated along the coast; native Irish Catholic population, particularly inland; mixed in Bushmills town itself
- **Religious denominations:** Church of Ireland (established church until 1869), Presbyterian (multiple congregations; numerically strong in north Antrim), Roman Catholic, Methodist. The population was overwhelmingly non-conformist Protestant and Catholic by denomination
- **Key historical events:** 1798 United Irishmen Rebellion (County Antrim was a principal theater; Battle of Antrim); Acts of Union 1800; Great Famine 1845–1852 and mass emigration; Disestablishment of Church of Ireland 1869

## Boundary changes

Billy civil parish was stable throughout 1780–1870. It sits within the barony of Dunluce North, which did not reorganize during this period.

The critical post-period split: after 1921 partition, County Antrim became part of Northern Ireland. Pre-1921 records for County Antrim can be held in either Dublin (NAI, Registry of Deeds, RCB Library) or Belfast (PRONI), depending on the record type. A researcher must check both cities' repositories; the partition did not move already-created records — it determined which new national administration inherited each class.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

**Start dates and levels** (established fact; FamilySearch Wiki page for Ireland vital records returned only generic content in this session):

- **Non-Catholic marriages:** civil registration began 1 April 1845, at the superintendent registrar's district level
- **All births, deaths, and Catholic marriages:** civil registration began 1 January 1864, at the same level

For 1780–1870 this means:

- Events before 1 April 1845: no civil records exist; church records are the only systematic source
- Non-Catholic (Church of Ireland, Presbyterian) marriages 1845–1863: registered at the civil registration district; the relevant district is Ballycastle or Coleraine (the researcher should verify which district covers the specific Billy townland)
- All births, deaths, and marriages from 1 January 1864 to 1870: registered and surviving

**Where held:** General Register Office of Northern Ireland (GRONI), Waterfront Plaza, 2 Malone Road, Belfast, BT7 1LT. Indexes are searchable free at https://www.irishgenealogy.ie.

**Gaps:** No civil records before 1845 (marriages) or 1864 (births/deaths). The researcher should not assume any birth or death record exists for the bulk of the target period.

### Church records

This is the **primary and most important record class** for 1780–1870 research in Billy civil parish, and the user's specific question about Church of Ireland registers is addressed here.

**Church of Ireland — Billy Parish**

The Church of Ireland parish of Billy is the ecclesiastical parish that maps onto the civil parish of the same name. The Church of Ireland was the established state church until 1 January 1871 (Disestablishment Act 1869), so its registers are the official record of baptisms, marriages, and burials for CoI members, and — under the Marriage Act — marriages of other Protestants were often conducted through it.

**State of the Billy CoI registers:** The 1922 burning of the Public Record Office of Ireland (Four Courts, Dublin) during the Irish Civil War destroyed approximately two-thirds of Church of Ireland parish registers that had been deposited there. However, many County Antrim CoI registers were **never sent to Dublin**. PRONI (Belfast) holds the primary collection of surviving County Antrim CoI registers on microfilm. Because Billy is in north County Antrim — an area where registers tended to remain locally or be filmed by PRONI before any Dublin deposit — the Billy CoI registers have a materially better survival prospect than registers from the Republic of Ireland.

**What to do:** Search the PRONI eCatalogue at https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/proni for "Billy" under Church of Ireland records to find the specific reference number (a MIC or CR class reference) and the date range of surviving baptism, marriage, and burial registers. PRONI will confirm whether the registers run back to 1780. Microfilm can be viewed in the PRONI public search room; reproductions can be ordered remotely.

Also check: The Representative Church Body (RCB) Library, Dublin (https://www.ireland.anglican.org/about/rcb-library) for any diocesan copies or registers held there rather than PRONI.

**Roman Catholic**

The RC parish(es) covering Billy civil parish (likely Ballintoy and/or Ramoan parish, Ballycastle) kept baptism, marriage, and burial registers. RC registers in rural north County Antrim typically begin in the 1820s–1840s; registers before about 1820 are rare in this area. The NLI Catholic Parish Registers project has digitized and made free online most surviving RC registers across Ireland: https://registers.nli.ie. Check both the Ballintoy and Ramoan (Ballycastle) RC parishes for coverage of Billy civil parish townlands.

**Presbyterian**

The Bush (Bushmills) Presbyterian congregation and neighboring congregations (e.g. Ballywillan/Portrush area) kept session books and baptismal registers. Presbyterian registers were never centralized to the Dublin PRO, so they are generally better preserved than CoI registers. PRONI holds microfilm of most County Antrim Presbyterian registers. The Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland (Records of Presbytery, Synod of North Ireland, and congregational records), 26 College Green, Belfast, is an additional repository.

**Methodist and other denominations**

Records vary by congregation and are held by the relevant denominational body or PRONI. Methodist circuit records are held by the Methodist Church in Ireland.

**Language:** All records in this area are in English.

### Census records

Ireland's census history is exceptionally difficult for the 1780–1870 period due to systematic destruction:

- **1813 census:** Taken but almost entirely destroyed (1922 fire)
- **1821 census:** Some County Antrim fragments survive at PRONI; largely destroyed (1922)
- **1831 census:** Largely destroyed; fragments in NAI for some parishes
- **1841 census:** Largely destroyed; some surviving household returns at NAI
- **1851 census:** Largely destroyed; some returns and statistical tables survive
- **1861 and 1871 censuses:** Deliberately pulped for paper salvage during World War I — no personal returns survive
- **1901 and 1911 censuses:** Survive in full (beyond the target period; very useful for working backward); free at https://www.irishgenealogy.ie

**Census substitutes — the most important sources for this period:**

| Substitute | Years | Coverage | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tithe Applotment Books | 1823–1837 | Heads of household (primarily Protestant-occupied land, but Catholic land included) | Free at IrishGenealogy.ie and FamilySearch |
| Griffith's Primary Valuation | c.1859–1861 (for Antrim) | Every household head; townland and property description | Free at AskAboutIreland.ie; Ancestry/FindMyPast |
| 1796 Flaxseed Premium Records | 1796 | Heads of household who grew flax; County Antrim covered | Free at PRONI eCatalogue / NLI |
| Poor Law rate books | From 1838 | Ratepayers by townland in each Poor Law Union | PRONI (in-person) |
| Estate rentals and surveys | Various | Tenant lists by townland; landlord-specific | PRONI estate papers |
| Old Age Pension claims | 1908–1922 | Includes census extracts for applicants born before 1864 | NAI / PRONI |

### Probate and court records

- **Pre-1858:** Probate was in ecclesiastical courts. The Consistorial Court of Connor (Diocese of Connor, which covers the Antrim area) handled smaller estates; the Prerogative Court of Canterbury handled higher-value ones. **Almost all original pre-1858 wills and administrations in Ireland were destroyed in the 1922 fire.** Surviving material: will indexes (the NAI holds the Will Book indexes for Connor diocese), will abstracts (Betham Abstracts at the NAI), and transcripts in various collections at NAI and PRONI.
- **Post-1858:** District Probate Registries (the relevant one was the Armagh District, which covered County Antrim) and the Principal Registry in Dublin. Records survive in better condition post-1858. PRONI holds Belfast District Probate Registry records.
- **Where held:** NAI (Dublin) for pre-1921 records; PRONI (Belfast) for Northern Ireland-specific court records; TNA (Kew) for some British-administered matters.
- **County Antrim Assizes and Quarter Sessions records:** PRONI.

### Land records

- **Survey system:** Townland system (Ireland's unique subdivision; below civil parish level). Metes and bounds descriptions in deeds.
- **Registry of Deeds, Dublin (from 1708):** Registered abstracts (memorials) of land transactions. Survives in full for the entire target period because it was never destroyed. The indexes (grantor/grantee) are on microfilm at PRONI; some are online. The Registry itself is at Henrietta Street, Dublin 1.
- **Estate papers (critical for tenant farmers):** Much of north County Antrim was landlord-owned. The MacDonnell family (Earls of Antrim) held large tracts. PRONI holds extensive estate collections including leases, rent rolls, surveys, and correspondence. For Billy civil parish, the relevant estate papers at PRONI should be identified through the eCatalogue under "Antrim" or "MacDonnell."
- **Encumbered Estates Court / Landed Estates Court (post-1849):** Created detailed estate maps and sale documentation during post-Famine estate sales; held at NAI and the Irish Land Commission records (NAI).
- **Land Commission records (from 1881, outside target period):** NAI; useful background.

### Military records

- **1798 Rebellion:** County Antrim was a major theater; muster rolls, transportation records, and other material at NAI, PRONI, and TNA.
- **British Army service records:** TNA, Kew (WO 97 for soldiers' documents; WO 76 for officers). Findmy Past and Ancestry have digitized many.
- **County Antrim Militia:** PRONI.
- **Royal Irish Constabulary (RIC, established 1822):** Service records at TNA (HO 184) and microfilm at NAI; some at PRONI.
- **Yeomanry records:** Relevant to the 1798 period; TNA and PRONI.

### Cemetery records

- **Billy CoI parish churchyard (Bushmills):** The Church of Ireland graveyard adjacent to the Billy parish church. Burial inscriptions should be checked via local surveys; some may appear on Find A Grave (https://www.findagrave.com) or BillionGraves (https://billiongraves.com).
- **RC burial grounds:** Associated with the RC parish(es) serving the area.
- **Presbyterian burial grounds:** Attached to the Bush and neighboring congregations.
- **Physical records:** Burial registers form part of the CoI parish register set at PRONI. Sexton records may survive locally.
- **Published surveys:** The Ulster Historical Foundation and local family history societies (North Antrim Family History Group, Moyle Historical & Genealogical Society) have conducted cemetery transcription projects.

### Newspaper records

Newspapers are a significant substitute source for death notices, marriage announcements, and legal notices throughout the 1780–1870 period.

- **Belfast Newsletter** (from 1737): Ireland's oldest newspaper; covers the whole of Ulster; birth, marriage, and death notices; legal notices; shipping lists (relevant for emigrant families). Available through British Newspaper Archive (subscription; https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk) and at Belfast Central Library and NLI.
- **Northern Whig** (from 1824): Belfast-based; good County Antrim coverage.
- **Coleraine Chronicle** (from 1844): Most directly relevant to north County Antrim and the Bushmills area for the latter part of the target period. Death notices and local affairs.
- **The Londonderry Sentinel** (from 1829): Northwest Ulster; relevant for families with Londonderry connections.
- **Where held:** British Newspaper Archive (subscription); Belfast Central Library newspaper collection; Linen Hall Library, Belfast; NLI, Dublin (microfilm).

### Immigration/emigration records

The period 1780–1870 saw continuous significant emigration from County Antrim — Ulster-Scots emigration to North America predated the Famine; the Famine years (1845–1852) saw a further wave.

- **Relevant ports of departure:** Belfast, Larne, Londonderry/Derry (the main Ulster emigrant port), Newry; Liverpool as the main transit port to North America.
- **Relevant ports of arrival:** New York, Philadelphia, Baltimore, Quebec (Canada), and Australian ports (assisted emigration schemes).
- **Record types:**
  - US passenger manifests (NARA; Ancestry has digitized; New York arrivals from 1820, Baltimore from 1820, Philadelphia from 1800)
  - UK Board of Trade passenger lists (from 1890 — mostly outside the target period)
  - Canadian passenger records (Library and Archives Canada)
  - Naturalizations: filed in any US court of record pre-1906; Declaration of Intent and Petition for Naturalization often name origin county
  - Passport applications: State Department records (NARA) from 1795; often name county of origin
- **Content note:** Passenger lists record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members.
- **Emigrant databases:** Ancestry.com, FindMyPast, and FamilySearch hold digitized passenger lists; the Famine Memorial databases at various NLI and NAI holdings name Famine-era emigrants.

### Tax records

- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837):** The primary tax-period record; functions as a census substitute. Free at IrishGenealogy.ie and FamilySearch.
- **Poor Law rate books (from 1838):** List all ratepayers in each townland within the Poor Law Union. The Billy civil parish area falls under the Ballycastle Poor Law Union. Rate books are at PRONI; in-person or reproduction access.
- **Griffith's Valuation (c.1859–61):** Also functions as a tax valuation; see Census section.
- **Hearth Money Rolls (1660s):** Pre-period but useful for identifying established family surnames in the county; some survive at PRONI and NAI.

### Other record types

- **1796 Flaxseed Premium Records:** The Irish Linen Board paid a premium to households growing flax; County Antrim is well covered. Lists household heads by townland. Free through PRONI eCatalogue and NLI.
- **Religious census of 1766:** In some parishes, householders were listed by religious affiliation; County Antrim coverage is partial. NAI and RCB Library.
- **Vestry records:** Church of Ireland vestry minutes record parish business and name churchwardens, overseers of the poor, and road overseers. PRONI.
- **Grand Jury presentments:** County Antrim Grand Jury records at PRONI; name contractors and local landholders.
- **National School records (from 1831):** National School roll books list pupils with ages and parents' names. Many survive at NAI; some at PRONI.
- **Estate maps:** Produced by landlords for their own management; often very detailed at townland level. PRONI holds many for County Antrim.
- **Local and county histories:** The Ulster Journal of Archaeology and various 19th-century county histories (e.g. George Hill's works) contain transcriptions of records and family accounts.

- **Pre-1864 births and deaths:** No civil system existed; only church records, which may or may not be digitized online (check PRONI eCatalogue and NLI registers individually)

## Known record losses

The 1922 Public Record Office of Ireland fire at the Four Courts, Dublin, is the central record loss for all Irish research. It destroyed:

- The bulk of Church of Ireland parish registers that had been deposited with the PRO (approximately two-thirds of all CoI registers for Ireland)
- Almost all original pre-1858 Irish wills and administrations
- The 1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851 census household returns
- Many estate and legal records

Additionally, the 1861 and 1871 census returns were deliberately pulped during World War I.

**Specific mitigation for Billy civil parish:** Because Billy is in County Antrim (now Northern Ireland), the most important CoI registers were more likely to have remained in Ulster rather than being sent to the Dublin PRO. PRONI has systematically microfilmed surviving Ulster CoI registers. The researcher should confirm the survival status of the Billy CoI registers directly with PRONI before assuming they were lost. The North Antrim area has relatively good CoI register survival.

**Substitute sources for destroyed records:**

| Pre-1864 civil births/deaths | CoI baptism and burial registers (PRONI); RC parish registers (NLI online); newspaper notices |
| Pre-1858 wills | NAI will indexes; Betham Abstracts (NAI); will abstracts at PRONI |
| 1821–1851 census returns | Tithe Applotment Books; Griffith's Valuation; estate rentals; Poor Law rate books |
| General parish membership | Griffith's Valuation entries showing religious denomination on houses |

## Research tips

**Note:** No Ireland-specific FamilySearch Wiki research-tips page content was returned by tools. The following tips are drawn from established Irish genealogical practice.

- **Establish the townland first.** Ireland's townland divisions (smaller than civil parishes) are the key geographic unit for most records. Use Griffith's Valuation at AskAboutIreland.ie to identify which townland(s) a family occupied, then use that townland in PRONI searches and estate paper searches.

- **Church of Ireland registers for Billy parish — check PRONI directly.** Search the PRONI eCatalogue under "Billy" for the MIC or CR class reference. The relevant Church of Ireland diocese is Connor (part of the Church of Ireland Diocese of Connor, now within the Down and Dromore & Connor Diocese). PRONI microfilms of Billy parish registers, if they survive, are the primary source for 1780–1844 baptisms, marriages, and burials for Church of Ireland families. Do not assume they were destroyed — verify with PRONI.

- **Do not conflate the Church of Ireland parish of Billy with the Roman Catholic parish serving the same area.** The civil parish of Billy and the CoI ecclesiastical parish of Billy share a name, but the RC population was served by one or more separately named RC parishes (likely Ballintoy and/or Ramoan). Search both church systems independently.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

---

> **Note on tool coverage:** The FamilySearch place authority tools (collections_search, volume_search, place_search) returned no results for Ireland and County Antrim in this session. The guide draws primarily on the FamilySearch Research Wiki's Ireland Church Records page and general Irish genealogical reference. Search the FamilySearch Catalog directly at https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog using "Billy, County Antrim, Ireland" for a complete picture of FamilySearch's microfilm and digital holdings.

---

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, County Antrim, Province of Ulster, Ireland
- **Location:** North Antrim coast, centered on Bushmills (~2 miles from the Giant's Causeway)
- **Barony:** Cary
- **Church of Ireland diocese:** Connor
- **Political status:** United Kingdom under the Act of Union 1800; after 1922, part of Northern Ireland (remaining in the UK)
- **Main national repository:** PRONI (Public Record Office of Northern Ireland), Belfast — not the Dublin archives
- **Ethnic/denominational composition:** Predominantly Ulster-Scots (Scots-Irish); Church of Ireland and Presbyterian were the majority denominations; Catholic minority (c. 40% of Northern Ireland population by 1861 per the FamilySearch Wiki)
- **Economy:** Agriculture (flax/linen), fishing, distilling (Old Bushmills Distillery), coastal trade
- **Key historical events:** 1798 Rebellion (County Antrim was a center); Act of Union 1800; Catholic Emancipation 1829; Great Famine 1845–1852; Land agitation 1850s–1870s

---

## Vital Records (Civil Registration)

| What | From | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Protestant marriages | 1 April 1845 | GRONI, Belfast; IrishGenealogy.ie |
| All births, marriages, deaths | 1 January 1864 | GRONI, Belfast; IrishGenealogy.ie |

**Coverage:** Civil registration covers only the last 6 years of the 1780–1870 window (Protestant marriages from 1845; everything else from 1864). For the full period before those dates, **church registers are the only primary vital record source**.

- **GRONI:** Oxford House, 49–55 Chichester Street, Belfast BT1 4HL
- **Free online:** https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/en/

---

## Church Records

This is the primary record class for 1780–1870. Critical: **two-thirds of all Church of Ireland parish registers were destroyed in the 1922 fire** at the Public Record Office in Dublin.

### Church of Ireland (Anglican)

> ⚠️ **Whether Billy's CoI registers survive must be verified before assuming availability.** It depends on whether they had been deposited in Dublin before 1922 or remained locally.

**To confirm survival — check both of these (cited in the FamilySearch Wiki):**
1. **PRONI's Guide to Church Records** (PDF): https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf
2. **RCB Library's List of Parish Registers** (PDF): https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf

**If registers do survive,** they typically include: baptisms, marriages, burials, vestry minutes, vestry cess (tax) lists.

**Where held (if extant):**
- PRONI — many CoI registers digitized: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni
- RCB Library, Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14 — library@ireland.anglican.org
- FindMyPast — "Irish Parish Register Baptisms, Marriages, Burials" (Ffolliott Collection, subscription)

### Presbyterian

- **Dominant denomination by membership** in north County Antrim. Multiple congregations likely served the Bushmills area.
- **Average register start date: 1830** (FamilySearch Wiki). The 1780–1830 portion of the target window is largely uncovered by surviving registers.
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, communicants rolls, session minutes. Burial registers are rare (the Wiki notes Catholics and Presbyterians "frequently do not contain burial registers").
- **Where held:** PRONI (microfilm and some digitized); Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland, 108 Botanic Avenue, Belfast BT7 1JT
- **Online:** FindMyPast — "Ireland, Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms / Marriages / Burials / Congregational Records" (subscription)

### Roman Catholic

- **Minority denomination** in the Bushmills area.
- **Register start dates:** Most rural parishes did not begin keeping records until Catholic Emancipation (1828–1830). Pre-1828 Catholic vital records rarely survive for rural north Antrim.
- **Important:** Catholic parish boundaries differ from CoI civil parish boundaries. The Catholic parish serving Bushmills may not align exactly with Billy civil parish.
- **Where held:**
  - NLI microfilm images (free, browse-only): https://registers.nli.ie/
  - Ancestry — "Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915" (collection 61039, indexed, subscription)
  - PRONI also holds some Northern Ireland Catholic registers

### Methodist

- Present in Ireland from 1746. Circuit records at PRONI and the Methodist Church in Ireland. Contact PRONI for what survives for the north Antrim area.

---

## Census Records

| Census | Status |
|---|---|
| 1813, 1821, 1851 | Destroyed in 1922 PRO fire |
| 1831 | Largely destroyed — **but partial County Antrim returns survive at PRONI** (unusual and valuable) |
| 1841 | Fragments survive |
| 1861, 1871 | Destroyed by government order |
| 1901, 1911 | Fully survived — free online at https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/ |

### Census Substitutes for 1780–1870

| Record | Period | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **Griffith's Primary Valuation** (all landholders/properties) | c. 1847–1864 | Free: https://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/; Ancestry (subscription) |
| **Tithe Applotment Books** (land occupiers liable to tithe) | 1823–1837 | Free: https://titheapplotmentbooks.nationalarchives.ie/ |
| **1796 Flax Growers List** (heads of household given spinning wheels) | 1796 | Various databases |
| **County Antrim partial 1831 census returns** | 1831 | Physical/microfilm at PRONI |
| **Poor Law rate books** (all rateable occupiers by Union) | 1838–1870 | Physical at PRONI |

---

## Probate and Court Records

- **Before 1858:** Ecclesiastical probate jurisdiction. Billy parish falls under the **Diocese of Connor** (Consistorial Court). **Most original pre-1858 wills and administrations were destroyed in the 1922 PRO fire.**
- **What survives:** Pre-1858 will and administration **indexes** survive, plus three major abstract collections:
  - "Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591–1866" — Ancestry, collection 62077 (subscription)
  - "Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866" — FamilySearch, collection 3460239 (free)
  - **Betham, Crossle, and Thrift Genealogical Abstracts** (pre-1922 copies of wills and other records) — FindMyPast (subscription)
- **From 1858:** Belfast District Probate Registry took over. Surviving records from 1858 at PRONI.

---

## Land Records

| Record | Period | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Estate papers, rent rolls, lease books | Ongoing from 17th c. | Physical at PRONI (catalogue online); not digitized |
| Tithe Applotment Books | 1823–1837 | Free online — see above |
| Griffith's Primary Valuation | 1847–1864 | Free online — see above |
| Registry of Deeds (voluntary registration of land deeds) | From 1708 | Physical at Registry of Deeds, Henrietta Street, Dublin 1; partial indexes online |
| Poor Law rate books | 1838–1870 | Physical at PRONI |

**Note on townlands:** Ireland organized all land records by **townland** (the smallest unit), not street address. Establishing which townland an ancestor occupied (from Griffith's or Tithe Books) is essential before searching estate papers, church registers, or locally organized series.

---

## Other Key Record Types

- **Military:** British Army records at The National Archives (TNA), Kew. Militia/yeomanry muster rolls at PRONI and TNA. 1798 Rebellion trial and arrest records at PRONI and TNA.
- **School records:** National School system from 1831. Registers at PRONI (some); inspectors' reports at National Archives of Ireland.
- **Newspapers:** *Coleraine Chronicle* (founded 1844) was the primary north Antrim paper; *Belfast Newsletter* (from 1737) also circulated. Available at British Newspaper Archive (subscription): https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/ and PRONI.
- **Emigration:** North Antrim was a major emigration source (Canada, USA). PRONI holds estate emigration lists. Ulster Historical Foundation database: http://www.ancestryireland.com/
- **Directories:** Pigot's (1820, 1824), Slater's, Bassett's County Antrim — list traders, professionals, and gentry in Bushmills.
- **Samuel Lewis, *Topographical Dictionary of Ireland* (1837):** Describes Billy parish including churches, schools, and local features as of 1837.

---

## Repository Summary

| Repository | Key holdings for Billy parish | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **PRONI**, 2 Titanic Boulevard, Belfast BT3 9HQ | Church registers (CoI, Presbyterian, Catholic); estate papers; Poor Law records; will indexes (post-1858); partial 1831 Antrim census; newspapers | In person or proni@communities-ni.gov.uk / +44 28 9053 4800 |
| **GRONI**, 49–55 Chichester Street, Belfast BT1 4HL | Civil registration births, marriages, deaths from 1864 (Protestant marriages from 1845) | In person or GRONI website |
| **RCB Library**, Braemor Park, Dublin 14 | Church of Ireland registers not at PRONI | library@ireland.anglican.org; https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy |
| **National Archives of Ireland**, Dublin | Tithe Books; 1901/1911 census; pre-1922 national records; will indexes | Free online + in person |
| **The National Archives (UK)**, Kew | British Army service/pension records; some Irish administrative records | In person + Ancestry/FamilySearch |
| **Registry of Deeds**, Dublin | Land deeds from 1708 | In person; partial indexes online |
| **Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland**, Belfast | Presbyterian church records; congregational histories | In person |

---

## Records NOT Online

- CoI and Presbyterian registers not yet digitized by PRONI — microfilm or in person at PRONI or RCB Library
- Estate papers and rent rolls — physical at PRONI (catalogue online only)
- Poor Law rate books (1838–1870) — physical at PRONI
- Registry of Deeds pre-20th century — largely physical
- Vestry records (CoI local administration: ratepayer lists, vestry minutes) — physical at PRONI
- Militia/yeomanry muster rolls — physical at PRONI or TNA

---

## Known Record Losses

- **Two-thirds of Church of Ireland parish registers** — 1922 PRO Dublin fire. Billy's CoI registers may or may not have survived; **must be verified** (see links above).
- **Most original pre-1858 wills and administrations** — same 1922 fire. Indexes and abstracts survive.
- **1813, 1821, 1851 census returns** — 1922 fire.
- **1861 and 1871 census returns** — destroyed by government order.

---

## Research Tips

1. **Verify CoI register survival first.** Check PRONI's Guide to Church Records (PDF) and the RCB Library's register list before assuming Billy's Church of Ireland registers are available or lost.

2. **Search CoI registers regardless of denomination.** The FamilySearch Wiki recommends this explicitly: before the Marriages Act 1844, Presbyterian marriages in CoI churches were sometimes the only legally recognized form; Catholics occasionally appear in CoI burials.

3. **Catholic Emancipation 1829 is the practical start date** for most rural Catholic registers. Pre-1828 Catholic vital records for rural north Antrim rarely exist.

4. **Presbyterian registers average 1830 start date.** For 1780–1830, session minutes and communicants rolls may survive where baptism/marriage registers do not.

5. **Griffith's and Tithe Books are the essential census substitutes.** Destroyed censuses mean these two property surveys are the primary tools for locating Antrim families in this period. Use together: Tithe Books for 1823–1837, Griffith's for 1847–1864.

6. **County Antrim's partial 1831 census returns at PRONI are unusual.** This survives for Antrim when almost no other Irish county has it — check it.

7. **Poor Law rate books fill the 1838–1847 gap** between Tithe Books and Griffith's. Annual occupier lists at PRONI.

8. **Know the townland first.** Every church and land record in Ireland is organized by townland. Griffith's Valuation is the standard starting point for identifying which townland a family occupied.

9. **Catholic and CoI parish boundaries differ.** If the expected Catholic parish yields nothing, search the registers of adjoining civil parishes.

10. **North Antrim emigration was extensive.** If an ancestor disappears after a certain date, consider emigration to Canada (Ontario, New Brunswick) or the US. PRONI holds estate emigration lists; the Ulster Historical Foundation (http://www.ancestryireland.com/) specializes in Ulster emigration records.

---

**Recommended first steps:** (1) Download PRONI's Guide to Church Records PDF and the RCB Library's register list to determine whether Billy's Church of Ireland registers survived 1922 and from what date. (2) Search Griffith's Valuation to anchor the family in a specific townland. (3) Search the Tithe Applotment Books for the 1823–1837 window. (4) Check PRONI's digitized church records portal for any available registers for the Bushmills/Billy area. (5) Consult the partial 1831 County Antrim census returns at PRONI.

- **Civil parish:** Billy, County Antrim, Province of Ulster, Ireland (United Kingdom from 1800)
- **Location:** North Antrim coast, centered on the town of Bushmills; approximately 2 miles from the Giant's Causeway
- **Barony:** Cary (the sub-county division in which Billy parish sits)
- **County seat:** Antrim town (county administrative center)
- **Church of Ireland diocese:** Connor (Diocese of Connor, which covers north County Antrim)
- **Political status during period:** Part of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland under the Act of Union 1800. After 1922, County Antrim became part of Northern Ireland (remaining in the UK). Per the Ireland Church Records wiki page: "six of the nine counties forming the province of Ulster (Antrim, Armagh, Down, Fermanagh, Londonderry, and Tyrone) voted to remain part of the United Kingdom." The two national record offices — PRONI in Belfast and the National Archives of Ireland in Dublin — each received copies of many pre-1922 national records.
- **Population during period:** A population figure specific to Billy civil parish was not returned by any tool in this session (place_population returned no results for Ireland).
- **Economy:** Agriculture (flax growing for the linen industry was the dominant occupation); fishing; distilling (Old Bushmills Distillery, on the Bush River, is one of the oldest licensed distilleries in Ireland); some coastal trade through Bushmills and nearby ports
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly Ulster-Scots (Scots-Irish) and Anglo-Irish settlers; Catholic minority. The Ireland Church Records wiki page notes that in Northern Ireland "the Church of Ireland and various aspects of the Presbyterian Churches were the dominant religions, accounting for sixty-percent of the population in 1861. While Catholics were a minority, they accounted for forty-percent of the population."
- **Religious denominations present:** Church of Ireland (established church); Presbyterian (various congregations; dominant denomination by membership in north Antrim); Roman Catholic; Methodist (present in Ireland from 1746 per the wiki page)
- **Key historical events in period:** 1798 United Irishmen Rebellion (County Antrim was a significant center; arrests, trials, and forfeitures); Act of Union 1800; Catholic Emancipation 1829; Great Famine 1845–1852 (severe effects throughout Ulster, including emigration); Land agitation and tenant-right movement throughout the 1850s–1870s

## Boundary changes

- Billy civil parish was a stable jurisdiction within County Antrim throughout 1780–1870; no boundary changes affected it during this period.
- The Act of Union 1800 transferred the Irish Parliament's powers to Westminster but did not alter county or parish boundaries.
- After 1922, record custody changed: records created or held in Belfast/County Antrim went to PRONI; copies of many all-Ireland records (civil registration, census) are held at both PRONI and the National Archives of Ireland. Church records for this area are primarily at PRONI and the RCB Library in Dublin.

## Available record types

For each record type, the holding level is stated as given by the tool result or the Ireland Church Records wiki page.

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Start dates by level:**
  - Protestant marriages only: civil registration began 1 April 1845, at the district (Superintendent Registrar's District) level
  - All births, marriages, and deaths (all denominations): civil registration began 1 January 1864, at the district level
  - The FamilySearch Ireland Church Records wiki page states: "Before civil registration was introduced in 1864, Church records provide the primary source for providing baptism, marriage and burial dates."
- **Coverage within 1780–1870:** Civil registration covers only the last 6 years of the target window (1864–1870). Protestant marriages are documented in civil records from 1845. For the entire window before those dates, no civil vital records exist — church registers are the only primary vital record source.
- **Where held:** General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI), Oxford House, 49–55 Chichester Street, Belfast BT1 4HL. Civil records from 1864 to 1921 are also available via IrishGenealogy.ie (https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/en/) for some counties; Northern Ireland records post-1922 are solely at GRONI.
- **Digitization level:** Indexed + images online for many years via IrishGenealogy.ie and Ancestry; others require in-person or copy request from GRONI.

### Church records

This is the primary record class for 1780–1870 in Billy parish. The Ireland Church Records wiki page is the source for all statements in this section (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records).

**Church of Ireland (Anglican/Episcopalian)**
- Per the wiki page: "Church of Ireland Records began in 1536, but two-thirds were destroyed in 1922." The destruction occurred in the fire at the Public Record Office in Dublin on 30 June 1922, which burned parish registers that had been deposited there. County Antrim parishes were not exempt: registers deposited in Dublin were lost regardless of the county they covered.
- **Critical point for this guide:** Whether the Billy/Bushmills Church of Ireland registers survive, and from what date, cannot be confirmed from the tool results returned in this session. The answer depends on whether Billy's registers had been deposited in Dublin before 1922 or remained at the vestry or a local repository.
- **To establish availability:** Consult two authoritative sources, both cited in the Ireland Church Records wiki page:
  1. **PRONI's Guide to Church Records** (PDF: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) — lists what church records exist for each parish in Northern Ireland, their date ranges, and whether PRONI holds them on microfilm or original form.
  2. **RCB Library's List of Parish Registers** (PDF: https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf) — lists Church of Ireland registers held at the RCB Library in Dublin, organized by diocese and parish.
- **If registers do survive:** Typical CoI record types are baptism registers, marriage registers, burial registers, vestry minute books, and vestry cess (local tax) lists.
- **Where held (if extant):** PRONI (for Northern Ireland) and/or RCB Library (Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14, email: library@ireland.anglican.org). PRONI has digitized a subset of CoI registers — see https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni.
- **FindMyPast** holds the Irish Parish Register Baptisms & Confirmations, Marriages, and Burials (Ffolliott Collection) — CoI records indexed at FindMyPast (subscription, cited in the wiki page).
- **Digitization level:** Where digitized by PRONI — indexed + images online. Other surviving registers: microfilm at PRONI or physical only at PRONI/RCB Library.
- **Language:** English

**Presbyterian**
- Per the wiki page: "In 1605 Scottish estate owners resettled mostly Presbyterian tenants from their estates to newly established estates in Northern Ireland. Numerous registers date from the 1600s, but the average starting date for these registers is 1830."
- Presbyterian was likely the denomination of the largest part of the population in Billy parish. There were likely multiple Presbyterian congregations serving Bushmills and surrounding townlands.
- Pre-1830 Presbyterian events (spanning most of the 1780–1830 portion of the target window) may not be in surviving registers and may require session minutes or other sources.
- **What to look for:** Baptism registers, marriage registers, communicants rolls, session minutes. The wiki page notes that "Catholic and Presbyterian church registers frequently do not contain burial registers."
- **Where held:** PRONI holds Presbyterian registers for Northern Ireland, many on microfilm. Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland, Union Theological College, 108 Botanic Avenue, Belfast BT7 1JT, also holds records. PRONI's Guide to Church Records lists what exists by congregation.
- **Online:** FindMyPast holds "Ireland, Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms," "Ireland, Non-Conformist Burials," "Ireland, Non-Conformist Congregational Records," and "Ireland, Non-Conformist Marriages" (all index, subscription, cited in the wiki page).
- **Digitization level:** Varies by congregation — some indexed + images at PRONI online; others microfilm or physical only at PRONI.

**Roman Catholic**
- Per the wiki page: "Ireland Catholic Church Records began from the mid 1700s. Most rural parishes did not start keeping records until Catholic Emancipation in 1828. Many of the city registers date from the 1750's."
- Catholics were a minority in north Antrim. Catholic registers for the Billy/Bushmills area likely begin in the late 1820s or early 1830s.
- **Important:** Catholic parish boundaries differ from Church of Ireland civil parish boundaries. The Catholic parish serving Bushmills may not align exactly with Billy civil parish and may span into adjacent civil parishes.
- **Where held:** National Library of Ireland (NLI) at https://registers.nli.ie/ (free microfilm images). Ancestry holds "Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655-1915" (collection 61039, index & images, subscription, cited in the wiki page). PRONI also holds some Catholic registers for Northern Ireland parishes.
- **Digitization level:** Images online at NLI (browse-only microfilm scans, no name index); name-indexed at Ancestry (subscription).

**Methodist**
- Per the wiki page: "A Methodist society began in Dublin in 1746." Methodism was present in Ireland from the mid-18th century.
- Methodist circuit records survive at varying levels; contact PRONI and the Methodist Church in Ireland for records covering the north Antrim area.

### Census records

- **1813, 1821, 1831, 1841, 1851 censuses:** Largely or entirely destroyed. The 1813, 1821, and 1851 originals burned in the 1922 PRO fire. The 1861 and 1871 census returns were destroyed by government order. Substantial fragments of the 1841 and 1851 survive.
- **County Antrim 1831 partial survival:** Some enumerators' returns for County Antrim survive for 1831; these are held at PRONI and are an unusually valuable source for this county and period.
- **1901 and 1911 Irish censuses:** Fully survived and freely searchable at https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/. These post-date the target period but provide family compositions, ages, and birthplaces to anchor backward research.
- **Census substitutes for 1780–1870:**
  - **Griffith's Primary Valuation (c. 1847–1864):** Comprehensive survey of all landholders and their properties across Ireland. This is the single most important census substitute for locating families in County Antrim during the target period. Freely available at https://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/ and at Ancestry (subscription).
  - **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837):** Lists all occupiers of land liable to pay tithes to the Church of Ireland — covers the target window well. Available free at https://titheapplotmentbooks.nationalarchives.ie/ (National Archives of Ireland).
  - **1796 Flax Growers List:** Lists heads of household in counties including Antrim who received spinning wheels for flax growing. Available through various databases.
  - **Hearth Money Rolls and Muster Rolls:** 17th-century tax and military lists; predates the target window but can establish family presence in townlands.
- **Digitization level (census substitutes):** Griffith's and Tithe Books — indexed + images online (free). 1831 Antrim fragments — physical/microfilm at PRONI.

### Probate and court records

- **Before 1858:** Probate jurisdiction was ecclesiastical. The Prerogative Court of Armagh handled estates with property in more than one diocese. The Consistorial Court of Connor handled smaller estates entirely within the Diocese of Connor (Billy parish falls within this diocese). **The vast majority of pre-1858 original probate records — wills and administrations — were destroyed in the 1922 PRO fire.**
- **Indexes survive:** The pre-1858 will and administration indexes survive. The FamilySearch Ireland Church Records wiki page cites:
  - "Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591-1866" at Ancestry (collection 62077, index & images, subscription)
  - "Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623-1866" at FamilySearch (collection 3460239, indexed + images, free)
- **Pre-1922 abstracts:** The wiki page also cites three collections of abstracts of records made before 1922:
  - Betham Genealogical Abstracts at FindMyPast (subscription)
  - Crossle Genealogical Abstracts at FindMyPast (subscription)
  - Thrift Genealogical Abstracts at FindMyPast (subscription) — "Records include wills, parish registers, freeman lists, and pedigree charts. Records date as far back as the 16th century."
- **From 1858:** District Probate Registries took over; the relevant registry for County Antrim was Belfast. Surviving records from 1858 onward are at PRONI.
- **Testate vs. intestate:** Wills exist only for those who left them (testate); for those who died without a will (intestate), search administration records in the same indexes.

### Land records

- **Survey system:** Ireland used the townland as the smallest land unit. Records are described by townland, civil parish, barony, and county — not by lot or section number.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Under the landlord system dominant in County Antrim throughout 1780–1870, large estate owners (often absentee) held land and collected rents. The land-granting authority was the Crown (for original grants) and individual landlords (for tenancy agreements). Estate papers — rent rolls, lease books, tenancy correspondence — are the primary pre-1823 land source for most Antrim families.
- **Where estate papers are held:** PRONI holds many large estate collections for County Antrim. The PRONI online catalogue identifies which family estate papers survive and what they contain.
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837):** Lists all occupiers of rateable land; the key mid-period land/census substitute. Free online at https://titheapplotmentbooks.nationalarchives.ie/.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847–1864):** Comprehensive property survey; the most reliable mid-to-late period land record. Free at https://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/; also on Ancestry.
- **Registry of Deeds (from 1708):** Voluntary registration of deeds in Dublin; covers some Antrim land transactions from the early 18th century. Held at the Registry of Deeds, Henrietta Street, Dublin 1. Indexes partially available online; originals physical only.
- **Digitization level:** Griffith's and Tithe Books — indexed + images online (free). Estate papers — physical at PRONI (some catalogued online). Registry of Deeds — largely physical; some indexes online.

### Military records

- **Relevant conflicts:** 1798 United Irishmen Rebellion (County Antrim was a significant center); Napoleonic Wars (British Army service); Crimean War (1853–1856); various militia and yeomanry service
- **British Army service records:** Held at The National Archives (TNA), Kew, London. Many pre-1913 records were destroyed in the 1940 Luftwaffe bombing of the record storage facility. Surviving records at TNA are available in part via Ancestry (subscription) and the Soldiers of the World War I collection at FamilySearch.
- **Militia and yeomanry:** County Antrim had active units, especially during the 1798 period. Muster rolls may survive at PRONI; some material at TNA.
- **1798 Rebellion records:** Records of arrests, trials, court martials, and forfeitures may exist at PRONI and TNA. A significant number of County Antrim men were tried after the 1798 rising.
- **Pension records:** Royal Chelsea Hospital pension records at TNA; some local pension papers at PRONI.

### Cemetery records

- **Church of Ireland churchyards:** Billy parish church and any chapels of ease would have associated burial grounds. Sexton records, where they survive, are held at PRONI with the other church records.
- **Presbyterian and Catholic burial grounds:** Many Presbyterians and Catholics were buried in CoI churchyards; also in denominational burial grounds associated with their own meeting houses/chapels.
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave (https://www.findagrave.com) and BillionGraves (https://billiongraves.com) have coverage for some County Antrim churchyards, but this is very uneven and far from comprehensive for the north Antrim area.
- **Graveyard transcription projects:** The North Antrim branch of the North of Ireland Family History Society and local genealogical societies have carried out graveyard surveys; results may be held at PRONI, local libraries, or society publications.
- **Digitization level:** Physical only or partial transcriptions (browse-only online where posted).

### Newspaper records

- **Local papers:** The Coleraine Chronicle (founded 1844) was the primary newspaper for the north Antrim area including Bushmills; it published obituaries, marriage notices, legal notices, and local news. Earlier papers serving the region include the Belfast Newsletter (founded 1737), which circulated across County Antrim.
- **Where held:** The British Newspaper Archive (https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/, subscription) holds a large collection of Irish provincial papers including north Antrim titles. PRONI holds physical runs of local papers. The National Library of Ireland also holds newspaper collections.
- **Content value:** Obituaries (often giving townland of origin, relatives' names, cause of death); marriage notices; land sale advertisements; legal notices including probate; news of emigration parties

### Immigration/emigration records

- **Significance:** North County Antrim was a major source of emigration to North America throughout the 18th and 19th centuries, particularly to Canada (Ontario, New Brunswick) and the United States (especially Pennsylvania and the Carolinas in the 18th century). Emigration intensified after the Famine.
- **Relevant ports:** Belfast, Londonderry (Derry), and smaller coastal ports were the main departure points from County Antrim.
- **Departure records:** PRONI holds surviving departure lists and some emigrant lists compiled by landlords or local agents. Some estate papers include emigration lists.
- **US arrival records:** Passenger arrival manifests for US ports are at NARA and available via Ancestry and FamilySearch. Coverage is denser from the 1820s onward.
- **Canada:** Library and Archives Canada has passenger lists and other immigration records for arrivals in Canadian ports (https://www.bac-lac.gc.ca/).
- **Naturalizations:** Declarations of intention and naturalization petitions filed in any US court of record are relevant for those who emigrated. Pre-1906 naturalizations can appear in any federal, state, or local court.
- **Ulster Historical Foundation:** The Ireland Church Records wiki page specifically cites the Ulster Historical Foundation (http://www.ancestryireland.com/) as a major database for Ulster emigration and church records.

### Tax records

- **Hearth Money Rolls (1660s–1669):** Lists Ulster households by number of hearths; predates the target window but useful for establishing family presence in townlands. Some County Antrim rolls survive.
- **Poll Tax / Subsidy Rolls (various 17th–18th century):** Survive for some periods; held at PRONI and National Archives of Ireland.
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837):** As noted above — key source for the target period, free online.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847–1864):** Property valuation — as noted above.
- **Poor Law rate books:** The Poor Law Union system introduced in 1838 created rate (tax) assessment books listing all rateable occupiers. These cover the later part of the target period (1838–1870) and are held at PRONI for County Antrim unions.
- **Digitization level:** Tithe Books and Griffith's — indexed + images online (free). Poor Law rate books — physical at PRONI; some may be microfilmed.

### Other record types

- **Flax growers lists (1796):** Significant for County Antrim, which was a major linen-producing county. Lists heads of household who received spinning wheels.
- **School records:** The National School system was established in Ireland in 1831. School registers survive in variable condition; PRONI holds many County Antrim National School records. The National Archives of Ireland holds inspectors' reports. Some records are at local schools.
- **Estate papers and rent rolls:** For families who were tenants on large estates (which describes most of the farming population in north Antrim), landlord estate papers are a critical source for identifying family members, recording tenancy changes, and noting deaths, marriages, or emigration. PRONI holds many large Antrim estate collections.
- **Directories:** Pigot's Directory (1820, 1824), Slater's Directory (various editions), and Bassett's County Antrim directory list traders, professionals, and gentry in Bushmills and surrounding areas. These are periodical snapshots, not comprehensive population lists.
- **Published county histories:** Samuel Lewis's *Topographical Dictionary of Ireland* (1837) describes every civil parish including Billy and lists churches, schools, and local features as of that date. Useful reference context.
